decisionsTitle: A release no longer stops on the runners' package archive, nor on a random id
decisionsSection:
**What happened, 2026-11-11.** The release of BR-V4.39 from the phone stopped twice in one afternoon, and neither stop was the code's.

**The package archive.** From 14:08 UTC GitHub's runners could not resolve Ubuntu's package hosts — the archive, its Azure mirror and the security host — for over two hours, while every other host they needed answered. All twelve `e2e` shards stopped in `yarn playwright install-deps chromium`, ten minutes in, before any test ran, on four attempts. The runner's image had not changed: the same `ubuntu-26.04` image, version `20261101.186.1`, had passed the same step in eight seconds at 11:51 UTC. What apt wanted and could not fetch were nine packages, all of them fonts: `fonts-ipafont-gothic`, `fonts-freefont-ttf`, `fonts-tlwg-loma-otf`, `fonts-unifont`, `fonts-wqy-zenhei`, `xfonts-encodings`, `xfonts-utils`, `xfonts-cyrillic` and `xfonts-scalable`.

**The owner**, asked whether to change the checks or to wait for the runners: «Da, fă-o și livrează».

**Decision.** With the browser cached, the step that installs Chromium's system packages has 150 seconds, and its failure is a warning, not a stop (`.github/workflows/docs-check.yml`, the `e2e-shard` job). The image already carries Chromium's libraries, since it ships a Chrome; what apt adds are fonts for Japanese, Chinese and Thai text and two fallback sets, which no page of the site uses. A library that is really missing fails the first test, loudly, so green still means the browser tests ran and passed. The browser tests passed on the first run with the change, and the release went on.

**The random id.** That run then went red on one unit shard. `tests/integration/registrations/elite-list.test.ts` checks that the trail of a deleted elite line never holds the race number typed, «4321», and it searched the whole serialized trail — which holds the rows' own ids, random hex. A staff id drawn in CI read `…143217…`. The ids are now replaced before the search, as `tests/integration/group-run-declarations/minor.test.ts` already did for its year. One re-run of the failed jobs passed.

**For the next time a release stops on a check that is not the code's.** GitHub refuses to re-run failed jobs while the run is still in progress, so the re-run waits for the run's other jobs; the label `ship` comes off at every stop (§658) and goes back on after the re-run is queued, since ship waits for the checks to settle.

**Refused.** Pinning the runner's image: it had not changed. Caching apt's packages: a second cache to keep, for nine fonts. Skipping the browser tests on a release: never. Bounding the same step in the two nightly workflows (`date-nightly.yml`, `e2e-dev-nightly.yml`): a nightly run that stops on the archive costs nothing and says the archive is away.
changelogLine: - **CI** — a release no longer stops when Ubuntu's package archive does not answer the runners: with the browser cached, the step that installs its system packages has 150 seconds and its failure is a warning. And the elite list's trail test no longer trips on a random id. §NNN.
batchLine: CI: a bounded `playwright install-deps`, and the elite list's trail test without its random ids
